headline: High: shared filesystem plus broad network and server-side command execution create dangerous default pathways for leakage, conflict, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat and n8n can bridge through the filesystem: Mentat has shared-state via filesystem and reads/writes files, while n8n can read/write the server filesystem and orchestrate tools. That creates a plausible path for attacker-controlled file content from one agent to influence the other, though not a direct default parser hijack.
conditions: IF n8n writes Mentat-consumed files into a shared directory, prompt-like content can steer Mentat
IF Mentat reads workflow-generated files as instructions, injected text can influence its edits
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Add a manual review step before Mentat consumes n8n outputs
Prefix workflow artifacts with non-instructional schemas
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags on shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code in selected files and has broad network egress; n8n processes whatever the workflow processes and can access the server filesystem plus many integrations. A shared filesystem or workflow handoff can move sensitive code or workflow data between them, creating default leakage risk beyond a single document.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace, code or workflow data can flow between them
IF n8n integrations send workflow contents off-box, Mentat-originated files may leave the environment
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Restrict n8n integrations to approved destinations
Disable broad egress where possible
Review shared files before either agent processes them
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on the shared filesystem

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted write access to the same filesystem surface, and Mentat can modify git state while n8n can execute server-side commands and write files. Concurrent edits or workflow actions can overwrite each other or corrupt repository state; the profiles explicitly describe shared state via filesystem and connected systems.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repo or directory, concurrent writes can conflict
IF n8n Execute Command touches files Mentat is editing, state corruption can occur
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories
Serialize access with a lock file
Disable Execute Command for shared repos
Commit or snapshot before handoff
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is an orchestrator that can act on workflow outputs, while Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals that may be treated as authoritative by downstream automation. Because n8n can execute commands and call integrations, a mistaken Mentat output can cascade into real actions without strong verification.
conditions: IF n8n consumes Mentat diffs without validation, incorrect edits can be executed downstream
IF a workflow turns Mentat output into commands or API calls, errors can propagate beyond code review
mitigations: Require human approval before execution
Validate diffs against tests or policy checks
Limit n8n to read-only review steps
Log and diff all handoffs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for Mentat outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat handles model provider API keys and source code, while n8n processes whatever the workflow processes and stores credentials on its server. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different retention/credential surfaces that can create compliance gaps if the same regulated data flows through both.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through n8n workflows, its server-side credential and logging surfaces may retain it differently than Mentat
IF source code or secrets are placed into shared workflow artifacts, retention policies may diverge
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of n8n workflows
Separate secret stores from shared files
Review retention settings in n8n
Minimize logged payloads
requires-engineering: document data-handling boundaries for both agents
